solution:
DIVYA has 5 letters D, I, V, Y, A, all different, and every one is used.
Number of permutations \(= 5! = 120\).
\(120\)

SHANTARAM has 9 letters, in which A occurs 3 times and the letters S, H, N, T, R, M occur once each.
Permutations of \(n\) objects of which \(p\) are alike \(= \frac{n!}{p!}\).
Number of permutations \(= \frac{9!}{3!} = \frac{362880}{6} = 60480\).
\(60480\)

REPRESENT has 9 letters, in which E occurs 3 times, R occurs twice, and P, S, N, T occur once each.
Number of permutations \(= \frac{9!}{3!\,2!} = \frac{362880}{6 \times 2} = 30240\).
\(30240\)

COMBINE has 7 letters C, O, M, B, I, N, E, all different.
Number of permutations \(= 7! = 5040\).
\(5040\)

BALBHARATI has 10 letters, in which A occurs 3 times, B occurs twice, and L, H, R, T, I occur once each.
Number of permutations \(= \frac{10!}{3!\,2!} = \frac{3628800}{6 \times 2} = 302400\).
\(302400\)

There are \(2 + 3 + 4 = 9\) books to be arranged in a row, but books of the same subject are identical, so interchanging them gives no new arrangement.
Number of distinct arrangements \(= \frac{9!}{2!\,3!\,4!} = \frac{362880}{2 \times 6 \times 24} = \frac{362880}{288} = 1260\).
\(1260\)

An outcome is a sequence of 8 results, and here 4 of them are H and 4 are T; the 4 heads are identical to one another and so are the 4 tails, so only their positions matter.
Number of ways \(= \frac{8!}{4!\,4!} = \frac{40320}{24 \times 24} = 70\).
\(70\)

At least 6 heads means exactly 6, 7 or 8 heads, and once the positions of the heads are chosen the tails fill the rest.
6 heads: \(\frac{8!}{6!\,2!} = 28\); 7 heads: \(\frac{8!}{7!\,1!} = 8\); 8 heads: \(\frac{8!}{8!} = 1\).
Number of ways \(= 28 + 8 + 1 = 37\).
\(37\)

There are \(5 + 4 + 4 = 13\) draws in all, and only the recorded sequence of colours matters, so marbles of the same colour count as identical.
Number of arrangements \(= \frac{13!}{5!\,4!\,4!} = \frac{6227020800}{120 \times 24 \times 24} = 90090\).
\(\frac{13!}{5!\,4!\,4!} = 90090\)

MATHEMATICAL has 12 letters, in which A occurs 3 times, M twice, T twice, and H, E, I, C, L once each.
Number of arrangements \(= \frac{12!}{3!\,2!\,2!} = \frac{479001600}{6 \times 2 \times 2} = 19958400\).
For all vowels together, tie the 5 vowels A, A, A, E, I into one block. The block and the 7 consonants M, T, H, M, T, C, L give 8 units in which M and T are each repeated twice, so the units arrange in \(\frac{8!}{2!\,2!} = \frac{40320}{4} = 10080\) ways, and inside the block the 5 vowels (A thrice) arrange in \(\frac{5!}{3!} = 20\) ways, giving \(10080 \times 20 = 201600\).
\(19958400\) arrangements in all, of which \(201600\) have all the vowels together.

MAHARASHTRA has 11 letters, in which A occurs 4 times, H twice, R twice, and M, S, T once each.
Number of arrangements \(= \frac{11!}{4!\,2!\,2!} = \frac{39916800}{24 \times 2 \times 2} = 415800\).
(a) For the R's and H's all together, treat the four letters R, R, H, H as one block. The block with A, A, A, A, M, S, T gives 8 units in which A is repeated 4 times, so the units arrange in \(\frac{8!}{4!} = 1680\) ways, and inside the block the four letters arrange in \(\frac{4!}{2!\,2!} = 6\) ways, giving \(1680 \times 6 = 10080\). Hence the arrangements in which R and H are never together \(= 415800 - 10080 = 405720\).
(b) For all vowels together, the 4 vowels are the four identical A's, so the block has only 1 internal arrangement. The block with the 7 consonants M, H, R, S, H, T, R gives 8 units in which H and R are each repeated twice, so the number of arrangements \(= \frac{8!}{2!\,2!} = \frac{40320}{4} = 10080\).
\(415800\) arrangements in all; (a) \(405720\); (b) \(10080\).

The word uses \(3 + 2 + 2 = 7\) letters in all, namely R, R, R, S, S, T, T, and letters of the same kind are identical.
Number of words \(= \frac{7!}{3!\,2!\,2!} = \frac{5040}{6 \times 2 \times 2} = 210\).
\(210\)

MUMBAI has 6 letters, in which M occurs twice and U, B, A, I once each.
B must be next to A, so tie A and B into one block; the stem does not say which of the two comes first, so the block can be AB or BA, that is \(2\) ways.
The block with the remaining letters M, U, M, I gives 5 units in which M is repeated twice, arranging in \(\frac{5!}{2!} = \frac{120}{2} = 60\) ways.
Number of arrangements \(= 2 \times 60 = 120\).
\(120\)
_note: The book's key gives 60. That value counts only one order of the pair (A followed by B). The stem asks for B to be next to A, which is satisfied by both AB and BA, so the block is orderable in 2 ways and the count is \(2 \times \frac{5!}{2!} = 120\). An exhaustive check of all 360 distinct arrangements of MUMBAI confirms exactly 120 have B adjacent to A, and exactly 60 have B immediately after A.

solution:
CONSTITUTION has 12 letters, in which T occurs 3 times, O twice, N twice, I twice, and C, S, U once each.
The word must begin and end with N, and there are exactly two N's; being identical, they can be placed at the two ends in only 1 way.
The remaining 10 letters C, O, S, T, I, T, U, T, I, O have T thrice, O twice and I twice, so they fill the 10 middle places in \(\frac{10!}{3!\,2!\,2!} = \frac{3628800}{6 \times 2 \times 2} = 151200\) ways.
\(\frac{10!}{3!\,2!\,2!} = 151200\)

ARRANGE has 7 letters, in which A occurs twice, R occurs twice, and N, G, E once each.
Number of arrangements \(= \frac{7!}{2!\,2!} = \frac{5040}{4} = 1260\).
For the second part, read the condition as excluding the arrangements in which the two R's are together and the two A's are together at the same time. Tying RR into one block and AA into another gives 5 units, namely the two blocks and N, G, E, all distinct, arranging in \(5! = 120\) ways (the two letters inside each block are identical, so a block has only 1 internal arrangement).
Required number \(= 1260 - 120 = 1140\).
\(1260\) arrangements in all, of which \(1140\) do not have the two R's and the two A's together.
_note: The book's key gives 1260, 1230 and the second value matches neither reading of the stem. Reading taken here: NOT (the R's together AND the A's together), which gives \(1260 - 5! = 1140\). Under the stricter reading (neither pair adjacent) the count is \(1260 - (360 + 360 - 120) = 660\), since arrangements with the R's together number \(\frac{6!}{2!} = 360\) and likewise for the A's. An exhaustive check of all 1260 arrangements confirms 1140 and 660 for the two readings respectively; 1230 arises from neither.

solution:
The six available digits are 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, and a 5-digit number uses five of them, so exactly one digit is left out. None of the digits is 0, so every arrangement is a genuine 5-digit number.
Leaving out a 2 gives the digits 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, yielding \(\frac{5!}{2!} = 60\) numbers; leaving out either 2 gives the same set, so this case is counted once. Similarly leaving out a 3 gives \(\frac{5!}{2!} = 60\).
Leaving out 4 gives 2, 2, 3, 3, 5, yielding \(\frac{5!}{2!\,2!} = 30\), and leaving out 5 gives 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, yielding \(30\).
Number of distinct numbers \(= 60 + 60 + 30 + 30 = 180\).
\(180\)

The 7 digits 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 are all different and all are used, so the number has 7 places.
The odd places are the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th, four in number, and the odd digits available are 3, 5, 7, 9, also four; so the odd digits exactly fill the odd places, in \(4! = 24\) ways.
The even digits 4, 6, 8 fill the three even places in \(3! = 6\) ways.
Number of distinct numbers \(= 24 \times 6 = 144\).
\(144\)

The number 659942 has the digits 6, 5, 9, 9, 4, 2, in which 9 occurs twice and the rest once each; none is 0, so every arrangement is a genuine 6-digit number.
Number of such numbers \(= \frac{6!}{2!} = \frac{720}{2} = 360\).
A number is divisible by 4 when the number formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4. From these digits the possible endings are 24, 64, 52, 56, 92 and 96.
For each of 24, 64, 52 and 56 the four remaining digits contain both 9's, giving \(\frac{4!}{2!} = 12\) numbers each; for 92 and 96 the four remaining digits are all different, giving \(4! = 24\) numbers each.
Numbers divisible by 4 \(= 4 \times 12 + 2 \times 24 = 48 + 48 = 96\).
\(360\) numbers in all, of which \(96\) are divisible by 4.
_note: The book's key gives 36, 84 and both values are wrong. The first is \(\frac{6!}{2!} = 360\), so the printed 36 has lost a zero. For the second, the six admissible endings are 24, 64, 52, 56, 92, 96, contributing \(12 + 12 + 12 + 12 + 24 + 24 = 96\); the key's 84 is short by exactly 12, which is one of the four endings that leave both 9's among the remaining digits. An exhaustive check of all 360 arrangements confirms 96.

solution:
INDIAN has 6 letters, in which I occurs twice, N occurs twice, and D, A once each.
Number of distinct words \(= \frac{6!}{2!\,2!} = \frac{720}{4} = 180\).
For the two N's together, tie them into one block; being identical they have only 1 internal arrangement. The block with I, D, I, A gives 5 units in which I is repeated twice, arranging in \(\frac{5!}{2!} = 60\) ways.
\(180\) words in all, of which \(60\) have the two N's together.

PLATOON has 7 letters, in which O occurs twice and P, L, A, T, N once each, so the total number of arrangements is \(\frac{7!}{2!} = \frac{5040}{2} = 2520\).
Tie the two O's into one block; being identical the block has only 1 internal arrangement, and the block with P, L, A, T, N gives 6 distinct units, arranging in \(6! = 720\) ways.
Number with the two O's never together \(= 2520 - 720 = 1800\).
\(1800\)

PLATOON has 4 consonants P, L, T, N, all different, and 3 vowels A, O, O, of which the two O's are identical.
With 4 consonants and 3 vowels in 7 places, the only alternating pattern is C V C V C V C, so the consonants take the odd places and the vowels the even places; there is just 1 such pattern.
The consonants arrange in \(4! = 24\) ways and the vowels in \(\frac{3!}{2!} = 3\) ways.
Number of arrangements \(= 24 \times 3 = 72\).
\(72\)
